findings.summary: The chapter's closing claim lost the phrase identifying it as the book's own.

evidence.baseline: Underneath all of this is a claim that the book is making and that the reader should be free to evaluate on its own terms, separate from any specific project's success or failure.
evidence.shipped: Underneath all of this is a claim the reader should be free to evaluate on its own terms, separate from any specific project's success or failure.

findings.diagnosis: That the book is making attributes the claim before granting the reader freedom to reject it, and the two halves are a matched pair: here is what I am asserting, and here is your standing to refuse it. Without the first half the claim has no owner, and the offer of evaluative freedom is made on behalf of nobody. The section is the volume's separation of its argument from its project, so naming who is arguing is the point.

findings.summary: The asymmetry sentence lost the repeated noun that made modernity the subject twice.

evidence.baseline: This asymmetry is not a side effect of modernity. It is one of modernity's defining features, and it is one of the central reasons the present civilizational moment has the shape it has.
evidence.shipped: This asymmetry is not a side effect of modernity. It is one of its defining features and a central reason the present civilizational moment has the shape it has.

findings.authorizedBy: Catalog 4.20, lexical monoculture, applied to the repeated modernity.
findings.diagnosis: Repeating modernity rather than pronominalizing is what makes the correction land: not a side effect of modernity but one of modernity's features. With its the reader must carry the antecedent across the full stop, and the contrast the sentence is drawing weakens to a distinction between kinds of relation. The second it is also doing work, since one of the central reasons is a separate claim from one of the defining features and the repeated pronoun keeps them parallel.

findings.summary: The list of what new signals would perceive gained a closing conjunction.

evidence.baseline: coordination signals that can perceive what current ones cannot: presence, regulation, relational integrity, ecological reciprocity, the conditions under which trust forms and intelligence remains in right relationship with life
evidence.shipped: coordination signals that can perceive what current ones cannot: presence, regulation, relational integrity, ecological reciprocity, and the conditions under which trust forms and intelligence remains in right relationship with life

findings.diagnosis: The baseline leaves the series open, which matters in a chapter whose argument is that nobody yet knows the full set of conditions a coherent civilization must perceive. Closing it with and implies the five are the list. This is the same operation the fishery narrative received in Chapter Four and the extraction enumeration in the same chapter, and it is the volume's most frequently repeated small loss.

findings.summary: The chapter handoff was split, converting one continuous movement into two destinations.

evidence.baseline: The next chapter turns to what happens when value learns to move along the lines of legibility this chapter has begun to describe, and to the actual experiments in regenerative economics that have begun, imperfectly and at small scale, to demonstrate that alternative pathways are real.
evidence.shipped: The next chapter turns to what happens when value learns to move along the lines of legibility this chapter has begun to describe. It also turns to experiments in regenerative economics that have begun, imperfectly and at small scale, to demonstrate that alternative pathways are real.

findings.diagnosis: Turns to X and to Y is one movement with two objects, which is how a chapter transition should read when the two are the same subject seen twice. It also turns makes them separate errands. Actual experiments is likewise the word that distinguishes the next chapter's evidence from this chapter's design space, and dropping it removes the contrast the handoff exists to set up.

openQuestions.question: Should the five The Larger Argument sections keep their distinct names?
openQuestions.context: The baseline uses one heading five times, so a reader learns that a section with that title is where the chapter steps back from its material to state the general claim. The pass named each separately, which reads better in a table of contents and loses the signal. This is the second of the volume's two recurring-heading families, alongside the five Providence disclosure sections. Recorded on each record; this is the first of the five.

regenerationTest.purpose: The rules must reproduce the section from the baseline without consulting the stored text.
regenerationTest.method: Derived from the immutable baseline applying editorial/method/standard.md, the corpus voice card, the volume-02 voice card, and the debt ledger under R-LEDGER-WINS.
regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required. F3 is worth recording because it is now the volume's most repeated single loss: an open series closed with a conjunction. It has appeared in the fishery narrative, the extraction enumeration, the crisis list, the Prologue's refusals, and here. Each instance is invisible on its own and the cumulative effect is a book that sounds more certain of its own completeness than it is, which is precisely the posture this chapter argues against.
